verdict.tagline: A brutal parry-focused adventure with stunning art and punishing bosses.
for_you_if: you love demanding parry-based combat systems
you appreciate hand-drawn comic book aesthetics
you want difficulty sliders to manage tough bosses
not_for_you_if: you dislike lengthy dialogue and cutscenes
you struggle with precise attack timing and patterns
you find sudden difficulty spikes frustrating

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as heavily focused on parrying mechanics, leaving alternative combat options with very little presence.

citations.review_text:
OVERRATED.
If you can buy it for 20 Eur or less, go for it, but i would not spend more than that.
It's a nice metroidvania, nice story, good world design, decent enemies variety, but it has 2 significant flaws imo:

1) Too much parry focused: in souls games, parrying is an option in your combat tool kid, created to enrich combat and to give you an additional mechanic to deal with certain attacks, but you always have the rest of the tool kit at your disposal if you decide not to focus on parry; spacing, dodge, dash, block, etc. 
In this game, you HAVE TO use parry, the other options are simply a minor presence into a combat designed to revolve around parry. This removes combat freedom of choices and it is not a good design choice.

2) The dialogs are WAY TOO long... the same story could be told in a  1/4 of the time and dialogues. It gets boring very fast and makes you want to skip though dialogues coz it slows down the pace and ruins the immersion.

The game looks really nice and the story really caught my interest at the beginning. However this isn't a normal metroidvania. It's just basically only "parry simulator." The combat is nothing but parry, parry, attack with zero variety. Enemies deal absurd damage and kill you in two hits if u again dont parry which is only thing you can do to cover demage. It isn't fun.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a lack of contact damage when touching walking enemies.

citations.review_text: i wanted this game for so long until i got it in summer sales i was so exited about this game and when i played it my face just went pale i put it to standard mode because i didnt think it would be that challenging because i have played hard games and i mostly dominate but this game was something else that i experienced i was the HARDEST GAME I HAD EVER PLAYED i could parry it was new to me and having no contact damage confused me and i was jumping over walking enemies. to any people that want to buy this game get it but be ready cuz i almost regreted buying this. W youtube tutorials

Havent played much yet but this game so far has been a really wonderful experience. The movement and parrying feels really good. The art style and animations are amazing and the story is interesting and really easy to follow unlike in hollow knight and the soulborne games where you need to fit puzzle pieces together for everything to make sense. One thing that gets me tho is that there needs to be a skip button for dialogue or cutscenes. Oh and also, theres no contact damage in this game. Thats all!!

Easily a 9/10 recommendation for people who love metroidvanias as well as parry mechanics.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game includes difficulty sliders for players who struggle with the challenge.

citations.review_text:
Even if you struggle with games like Hollow Knight, you should play this game - it has difficulty sliders and they SAVED me.
Oh but careful if you're sensitive about gore. Theres so much gore. And body horror. Its a lot. Its great tho.

Runs great on Steam Deck. The parrying is difficult at first, but becomes addicting once you get better. It has an easier mode thankfully for when things get too difficult or you want a smoother experience like I do. Combat and story are great and I love how colorful the world is outside of the dungeons you’ll spend most of your time in.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the attack hitboxes as misaligned with visual animations, leading to unexpected hits.

citations.review_text:
OK to set my opinion straight I really like the game, its awesome, but omg some of the things the game does just causes me to rage. Like that you cant dash mid air, but its an understandable thing, that some devs for their games may want, but you kind of get a mid air dash when you use the tailisman, so that's not to bad. But also I hate the stun that happens to you when you get hit multiple times, or what ever, because sometimes I slightly miss a "parry" (its not really a parry, because it does not go back to them, or we don't hit back for a true parry, so its more like a block) and it causes me to just get hit multiple times causes me to die, and that just feels just so unfair. And then the only way around it is by a locked ability that feels like it should just be a starting ability if they want it in the game. But the thing that just causes the most rage, is that the hit boxes are absolute buns, like I'll jump up like an entire body height, and still manage to be hit, like Lady Ethereal's like sweaping cut should only dammage the bottom area, so If I jump I should be perfectly fine right? NO, thats stupid aparently, fix the hitboxes for the love of everything that is good.

But overall I rate the game like a 8.5/10, but I still do have to finish the game, so I might add or remove things, and potentialy change my rating of the game overall.

A parry based combat system with no stagger mechanic and no i-frames is bad. Don't forget that when an enemy starts their attack animation they can still turn around and hit you, or maybe the attack hitbox will just hit you anyway. Everything kills you very quickly, and any enemy that staggers you is almost certain death. "skill issue" this "skill issue" that, I don't care, frustrating and mechanically unfun combat ruins this

The story seems interesting, but the dialogue is cliche, repetitive, long, and constant. 

Yeah there is the easy mode, but it takes all the reward out of defeating a boss all so you can get some half baked dialogue

maybe I will come back to this at some point but I was just not having a good experience

the game is challenging which is great. its too difficult to retain your winnings. you can get bosses to walk into lazers to kill them. controlling the character feels clunky. the save points are sometimes a loading screen away which is okay in an open world game but not in a linear game like this. the hitboxes on the attacks are not lined up with the animations which means sometimes i get hit when i dont see the weapon slash line up with me. i will put more time into playing the game before i complain that the combat is bad. there is a lot of dialogue in the game that doesnt contribute to anything and rehashes what i already know

claims.claim: Reviewers report that fighting multiple enemies at the same time is very difficult because the game only allows parrying one attack at a time.

citations.review_text: really tried to like it but this game is just bash your head against a wall simulator. ive beaten plenty of parry based games like sekiro, lies of p and e33 parry only so i feel like im pretty decent at parrying but nine sols is worse. basic enemies  have hard to read instant attacks that take away half your hp bar just on the runback to a boss. bosses have pretty weird and some inconsistent attacks that feel super bad to play into. directional parry really sucks in a game like this plus the fact you can only parry one thing at a time so the game completely falls apart if you're ever against more than 1 enemy. the art and story are cool, the map is alright and the bosses can be a cool spectacle but all that good wears off fast after dealing with all the other unpolished gameplay. i only reccommend this game if you need to waste your time

I want to like this game but it feels just it's just made to frustrate you. It feels like the enemies are made to frustrate you. Healing is quite difficult and unless you are perfectly parrying every hallway attack you have a pretty good chance of dying and losing all your money in a frustrating loop. 

Getting knocked down means you can't get up quickly again and will likely get hit in the same combo (there is an upgrade to help with this but still)

facing multiple opponents you can't parry all the attacks or punish the enemy when you do. Normally, that's more or less fine but this game isn't like hollow knight where you can just dodge them when they stack up. 

maybe I should just put it on easy but I don't want to play that way and I am not having fun playing it

I also don't think the platforming feels very good and the backgrounds within the same zones look very similar so I find myself not super knowing where I am. The mini bosses also feel like a load of crap.

edit: played it for a few more hours and had some passable experiences but can't really say I enjoyed any of it. Was just going through the motions. Hit another section and died several more times and thought 'nah I'm not having fun'. 

I kept hearing how good the bosses were so I just wanted to get to those parts. Of the ones I fought, I didn't really enjoy any of them though so not sure why I kept going. 

Respect to the developers though since the game looks good, sounds good, and when it works it works for what it wants to do. Apparently just not for me

Nine Sols is almost a great game. Unfortunately, the entire game requires parrying of attacks.

Now, don't get me wrong--I love Sekiro, I think it's the best single entry in the From Software catalogue. The problem is that Nine Sols doesn't quite match the fine-tuned combat that From are known for. There are plenty of attacks where the hitboxes extend far beyond where you would expect, with you often getting hit while standing behind enemies. On top of that, towards what I assume is the end of the early game you get what are known as "Unbound Counters" which are essentially super-parries. This enables you to parry a certain type of attack that previously you would have to dodge. However, these unbound counters require you to hold and then release the parry button, which makes precise timing difficult. In addition to this, many of the attacks that require this type of counter are so fast that unless you're just sat around waiting for an enemy to attack, you're almost certainly going to miss them as the telegraphing can be incredibly short.

I know that a lot of people love this game but ultimately it isn't for me. I really enjoy the way that Sekiro encourages you to mix defence in with offence, and Nine Sols does expand on that, but unfortunately you're pretty much discouraged from attacking, as that prevents you from doing what seems to be intended: sit there passively, waiting for attacks to parry then once you have enough Qi, hit them with a talisman and start waiting again. I don't find that super engaging.

Otherwise, this would be a pretty good metroidvania, I really like the map design (although some kind of player map markers would be nice) the art style is great, and the sound design is cool too. The plot is interesting, although there is a *lot* of dialogue which often feels a bit extra.

If I was able to give this a rating out of 10, it would probably get a 6, but I wouldn't recommend it unless you enjoy punishing games that require incredible refl…

Having loads of fun playing this at the moment. (Roughly 13hrs in right now)

The combat is very hard but very enjoyable and satisfying when you get used to the parrying mechanic.

Others may enjoy reading all the text which is completely fine. However, for me its a bit much.

Overall even with the large amount of dialogue the game provides, I would recommend giving Nine Sols a try for all players, new or experienced with metroidvania games. 
Just note that Nine Sols is a harder type of metroidvania, so new comers to this genre may want some practice with easier games before trying this one out first.

cohorts.summary: Later players praise the striking art style and gradual unlocking of fast travel, while pointing out a massive difficulty spike on the final boss and demanding combat patterns.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the final boss features a sudden and extreme spike in difficulty compared to the rest of the game.

citations.review_text:
An amazing game. The beginning was difficult for me i don't know why. I had to start this game three times before I finally got into it. I also had a problem with the fact that there was no colorblind option when the game first came out, but thankfully, they eventually added one.

I won't say that it's Hollow Knight combined with Sekiro, because that's how it might seem at first, but the game has its own soul and identity. The story is captivating, the graphics are gorgeous and will age incredibly well, and the combat is very satisfying.

The only thing I can criticize about this game is the final boss. The problem isn't the difficulty of the final boss itself, but the fact that the game doesn't prepare you for such a sudden jump in difficulty. Most games prepare you for the final battle throughout the entire adventure, but that's not the case here. You can feel like a god while fighting the penultimate boss, only to discover that the final boss isn't a wall, but a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ fortress.

Overall, a fun parry-slop game. Not a really an excellent game, but still worth a play through. Don't expect to be wowed, but if you like metriodvania games, you will probably like this.

The visuals are good, the music is forgettable though. I can legitimately only vaguely remember one song and that's only b/c it is for one of the harder bosses, so I heard it a lot. The visuals are reasonably pretty but there were a few moments where I wished that they had made things more saturated. Level visuals could have used a bit more variance b/c there were 3 areas which looked basically identical with the biggest difference being the color palette. I'd give it a combined B+ on the art direction.

Level design is fine overall. I was never impressed with it but, it is hard to see how I could be with how bog-standard it is. Compared to other metriodvanias, there is less backtracking over previous areas as new abilities are unlocked, which makes the areas all feel like isolated levels rather than part of a world. I'd give it a solid B for being hard to find something to say about it either way.

There is a big disparity between the difficulty of the final boss and everything else. It is extremely noticeable b/c the 2 penultimate bosses are relative pushovers compared to the one before them (they are 2 phase bosses which feels wrong at that point in the game) as well as feeling phoned in compared to the bosses before them. I'd give this an A- for boss design.

Unlocks of abilities in the game are very arbitrary and slapdash. Comparing to hollow knight, which is good about integrating acquiring abilities into the world, this game just randomly dumps you to into the same isolated minigame every time and has you run through it with minimal variation. It is just lazy. I'd give it a C- in this aspect.

The story is just mediocre. It is mostly a chinesse mythology based souls-alike. I didn't really enjoy the way that the characters backstories were just dumped unceremoniousl…

This is truly an amazing game. In terms of difficulty, I’d say it’s easier than Hollow Knight—except for the final boss - IT WILL KICK YOUR ASS A FEW TIMES AT LEAST. The final boss is a massive skill check that only lets you finish the game once you’ve truly mastered its mechanics. Chef's kiss tho

Story-wise, I would personally place it above even Hollow Knight. It’s genuinely one of the most inspiring and heartbreaking stories I’ve ever had the chance to experience. It’s a game that manages to challenge you mechanically while also telling a deeply emotional and memorable story.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat as heavily centered around a precise parry system that requires learning attack timings and patterns.

citations.review_text:
hollow knight attacked and nine sols parried it.

and i say that as someone with 100% in both HK and silksong.

the combat is EXCEPTIONAL. not "good for an indie game". genuinely elite. parry-focused, sekiro like, weighty, punishing. every boss is a dance - whether its a tango or a slow waltz. you dont just react; you learn tells, delays, fake-outs, the game is absolutely brutal but fair. zero artificial grind.

the worst boss in nine sols is better than the best boss in most metroidvanias. true ending [spoiler]eigong[/spoiler] genuinely nearly broke me. for sure rivals some of the hardest fights ive ever done, but its absolute CINEMA.

the exploration is classic metroidvania done RIGHT. ability gates, hidden paths, secrets everywhere. you start weak, lost, overwhelmed, by the end, your practically immortal. the world is smaller than a map like silksong but denser.

the story really surprised me. revenge, atonement, world-class writing. the end had me seriously emotional. im not proud of it but the story earned it. nine sols has that unique ability to make you truly attached to the characters, in a way that is almost unparalleled.

the art style is one of the best ive seen. taoist sci-fi (chinese devs for context), hand-drawn, comic book cutscenes, the sound design is excellent – not metro level, but excellent nevertheless.

in all honesty, the skill curve is sharp and not entirely balanced, and some enemies feel rigged.

if you liked hollow knight, buy this. if you liked sekiro, buy this. if you like not being the guy who misses out on peak gameplay due to skill issues, buy this.

stop reading. your skill issue isnt an excuse. buy it.

9.7/10.

I really wish Steam allowed "mixed" reviews because the story, art, and world-building are all top notch. It just came down to too much of the game focusing on the parry mechanic. By the end of the game, the boss fights consist of 75% parrying, which should tell you whether this game will be for you or not. It's well crafted, but ultimately not for me.  I got as far as the final boss before putting it down. 

If you enjoy parry-centric soulslike games, this will be up your alley. If that's not your thing and were coming for the metroidvania elements, I'd suggest staying away. Personally, I find the whole "miss one parry and lose 50% of your health" mechanic tiresome. Some people enjoy needing 50 attempts on a boss before winning, to each their own, but I don't have the time or the blood pressure for it.

This game reminds me of Sekiro, I think the story is very good, the visuals are beautiful, the NPC is also unique, there are many unique things about this game, but you need to remember before buying or playing this game, behind all that this game has its own mechanics, namely parry time, yes that's right parry like Sekiro but the 2D version play the standard difficulty mode and you will feel the sensation.

I recommend this game for metroidvania game lovers, the best game 10/10

claims.claim: Reviewers note that fast travel is initially restricted to the main hub and the last used point, with full node-to-node fast travel unlocked later in progression.

citations.review_text:
[b]This review will spoil some stuff in terms of progression. Also, this review will mainly focus on things that I didn't enjoy as I think the game is good overall.[/b]

A solid game for the most part. My main issue with the game personally is the way progression is handled. For example, the ability to air dodge and double jump are tied to mid and late game progression respectively. Not being able to air dodge at the beginning of the game hurts the movement for me personally and makes it feel sluggish for a good part of it until you get it.

Another issue with the game for me is fast travel. At the beginning of the game, once you unlock the main hub, you can only fast travel back to the hub and to the last used fast travel point. The ability to fast travel to ANY node is locked behind mid game progression and even then, you can only teleport to any node from the main hub, you can't use other nodes for it. Why? What's the point in this design decision other than to inconvenience the player.

Overall, I enjoyed Nine Sols quite a bit, but most of my enjoyment came from when I finally unlocked more movement options, as base kit Yi is sluggish and sometimes not fun to pilot. The art style is amazing, the music is phenomenal, the writing was good and made me invested in the story. 

Most of the bosses were fun (With the exceptions of the one in the Empytrean District and the final boss).

[b]TL;DR: 8/10 game with a few issue with progression that can make the game drag on more than it needs to[/b]

Incredibly touching, detailed and well thought-out story. Exploration is enjoyable, if tough at times, especially with how linear the area progression was for the first couple of zones, only really opening up for the 2nd and 3rd last zones. This also makes it difficult to replay the game, though theres plenty of content for your first playthrough. I had difficulty understanding a couple of the mechanics at first, (though i dont think it was the games fault that I couldnt figure out that you have to attack the shield holding guy with the shield piercing attack) and some of your moveset becomes obsolete depending on your playstyle (for example, the charged sword attack), but the add-ons/charms/jades rectify a lot of the issues you might have with your preferred fighting style not being represented. There is a heavy focus on understanding the parrying mechanic, which is a vital and core part of the gameplay, so if you arent good at timing this game might not be for you. Thankfully, this game loves not wasting your time. You're usually going to be short on jin, your money, but you always get just enough per expedition to make it worth your while. You also unlock a teleport between safe points/bonfires/spirit roots mechanic later in the game, once you're adequately geared to explore for collectibles. Speaking of the save points, there is more then enough of them everywhere, one being in every room/cell. The game understands that you're supposed to be weak and squishy and punishes you for dumb mistakes with death, not endless runbacks. The runbacks for bosses are effected by this aswell, all of them being shorter then 10 seconds. Moving on to the art direction- the music is fantastic, the themeing and art is wonderful and appeasing, and the implications of what is happening in the facility around you are equal parts horrific and intriguing, though I wont touch on examples as to avoid spoilers.

Overall, i must say this game is a 10/10, worth playing 20-50 hour solo expe…

This game isnt completely perfect, it has some flaws, but regardless this was a 10/10 for me.   

I will start with some of its flaws first.  
First, I enjoyed the map, I liked exploring around New Kunlun and learning how it came to be, the only flaw is that early on its not clear where you should be going, you may find yourself lost at some point unless unless you can remember where you can go now that you unlocked a new ability. I generally liked exploring the map so I didnt mind as much but I did have some moments where I was just walking around. It doesnt help you dont get fast travel until around half way through the game so you'll be walking around a fair bit. Whats also weird was the boss fights, some boss fights was easy, but some are crazy hard. I did the 3rd boss which was relatively easy but when i got to the 4th it felt like the difficulty jumped substantially. I really struggling with that boss and when i finally completed it, the bosses that came after felt loads easier (besides final)

The next is the parry system, no matter how you go about the game you need to be able to parry and im a bit mixed on it with some issues I have.  
It can be really difficult to tell when the parry timing is right depending on the monsters or bosses you face, each one has its own distinct timing but its not consistent with how you know its coming. for example, monster A might want you to parry as its arm is swinged down whilst the other is half way because he's faster. This is fine to an extent but theres no real indicator for you, you just have to go by feel which can be brutal because you will essentially need to die for you to get use to it. This is fairly normal in a souls like game though so I wasnt too fussed about this       

My second issue is the varying parry mechanics, there are 3 to keep in mind
normal attack - parry normally
red attack - jump and parry
projectile red attack - hold down parry button to deflect

problem 1 is that both red attack and project a…

the story really surprised me. revenge, atonement, world-class writing. the end had me seriously emotional. im not proud of it but the story earned it. nine sols has that unique ability to make you truly attached to the characters, in a way that is almost unparalleled.

the art style is one of the best ive seen. taoist sci-fi (chinese devs for context), hand-drawn, comic book cutscenes, the sound design is excellent – not metro level, but excellent nevertheless.

in all honesty, the skill curve is sharp and not entirely balanced, and some enemies feel rigged.

if you liked hollow knight, buy this. if you liked sekiro, buy this. if you like not being the guy who misses out on peak gameplay due to skill issues, buy this.

stop reading. your skill issue isnt an excuse. buy it.

9.7/10.

This game is incredibly good, the artstyle is gorgeous, the music is amazing, the characters are great and the gameplay is really smooth and fun. The world and theming of each region is super captivating and the story emboldens the whole experience.

I don't have many complaints but here are a few: The hitboxes on some attacks feel kinda whack, the jades seem pretty unbalanced with a lot of them being really bad while others are almost broken in how useful they are, and some enemies and bosses use tweening instead of cell animation and it's sort of distracting.

Overall It's an amazingly crafted experience that sits among the best medtroidvania's out there, 8/10
